title: Chapter 4 Quiz 4
description: Sorting by finding the smallest value again and again.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: What does **selection sort** do on each pass?
options: Splits the array into equal halves
Moves the smallest value into place
questions.explanation: It selects the minimum of the rest and puts it in place. Watch out: swapping neighbours is bubble sort.

questions.question: Put the steps of selection sort in order.
items: Traverse from the first to the second-to-last cell
Find the smallest element in the rest of the array
Swap it with the current cell
questions.explanation: Walk the array, find the minimum, swap, display at the end.

questions.question: Complete the selection sort.
questions.code:
For i From 1 To 4 Do
    minIndex ← i
    For j From {{1}} To 5 Do
        If tab[j] < tab[minIndex] Then
            minIndex ← j
        EndIf
    EndFor
    temp ← tab[i]
    tab[i] ← tab[{{2}}]
    tab[minIndex] ← temp
EndFor
questions.explanation: The inner loop looks at the rest after i. The swap uses temp, tab[i] and tab[minIndex].

questions.question: Sort [22, 7, 15, 3, 19]. Give the array after each pass of the outer loop (pass 1 to 4).
questions.explanation: Each pass places the smallest remaining value at position i. Watch out: the swap changes only two cells, the others keep their place.

questions.question: How many passes does the outer loop make for an array of 5 elements?
questions.explanation: i goes from 1 to 4. Watch out: the last element is already in place, so there is no fifth pass.

questions.question: For [22, 7, 15, 3, 19], what is minIndex at the end of pass 1?
questions.explanation: The smallest value, 3, is in position 4. Watch out: minIndex is a position, not the value 3.

questions.question: After pass 1 of selection sort, the smallest element is at position 1.
questions.explanation: That is exactly what each pass guarantees for its own position.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of selection sort given in the course?
questions.explanation: Two nested loops over the array give O(n²). Watch out: one loop alone would give O(n).

questions.question: This selection sort swaps tab[i] and tab[minIndex]. One line of the swap is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
temp ← tab[i]
tab[i] ← tab[minIndex]
tab[minIndex] ← tab[i]
questions.explanation: After line 2, tab[i] already holds the new value, so the old value of tab[i] would be lost. Watch out: the old value is saved in temp.

questions.question: This should sort the array in ascending order. One line is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
For j From i + 1 To 5 Do
    If tab[j] > tab[minIndex] Then
        minIndex ← j
    EndIf
EndFor
questions.explanation: We look for the smallest value, so the test is <. Watch out: with > the code finds the largest value and sorts in descending order.
